symptom: `mxcli check --help` offered `# Check syntax only (no project needed)  mxcli check script.mdl`, but run from a directory holding an .mpr it printed `Using project: ...\project.mpr (auto-detected in the current directory; pass -p to use another)` and resolved references against it; there was no way to get the advertised syntax-only check there
cause: `rootCmd.PersistentPreRun` auto-discovery sets `-p` before `check` runs, and `check` treats any project as an implicit `--references` (the fix for an unqualified `Check passed!`); the help example was only true outside a project directory
insight: Two individually right decisions (auto-detect the sole .mpr, mendixlabs/mxcli#1444; a project implies reference checks) composed into a help example that is false exactly where users run it — a project directory, which is also where the generated CLAUDE.md template told agents `check script.mdl # Syntax only`. Changing the default would have silently weakened every `cd app && mxcli check` that relies on the auto-detected refs, so the fix is an opt-out (`--no-project`, honoured by PersistentPreRun for any command that registers it), a notice on the auto-detect line naming it, a refusal when combined with -p/--references/--post-migration, and help/docs whose syntax-only example carries the flag. Note `Flags().Set` by auto-detection marks `-p` Changed, so a conflict check on Changed only works because discovery is skipped first. Test runs real main() in a temp dir with a non-project Stray.mpr (opening it would error); control: discovery forced on under --no-project prints the reported `Using project:` line
